summary: The draft's citation width is genuinely high (90 sources, all seven named clusters at least touched). The gaps are concentrated in one place: deliverable (iii)'s ranked recommendations name experiments and reframings without the motivating primary that the vault holds for each. Five of the eight coverage gaps below never appeared in ANY of the three angle drafts, so they are Layer-1-corpus-to-Layer-4 losses rather than synthesis compression; two (BCQ, Deep Kernel Learning) were present in draft-a and dropped by the synthesizer.

findings.location: Deliverable (iii), RANK 10 ('Reframe three results as refinements of named positions'), and/or (i).J (the Fannjiang item)
findings.issue: The Goodhart-taxonomy cluster is entirely absent from the report and from all three angle drafts. The paper's central diagnosis -- 'which off-distribution maximizers a surrogate's mean admits' -- has a precise, named, off-the-shelf category in the literature, and the report recommends citing Gao [54] for the degradation curves without noting that Gao's own decomposition is an application of that taxonomy. The query's deliverable (iii) explicitly hunts for 'a result explored but UNDER-EXPLAINED: a finding whose significance the paper states flatly and that the literature would let it frame more sharply.' This is the cleanest instance of that in the corpus and the report does not reach for it.
findings.evidence: Vault note `180304585-categorizing-variants-of-goodharts-law` (Manheim & Garrabrant, arXiv:1803.04585), tagged this pass. Its 'Extremal Goodhart -- Model Insufficiency' sub-case reads: 'the metric of interest is based on a learned relationship... approximately accurate in the initial region; selection pressure moves the metric away from the region in which the relationship is most accurate so that the relationship collapses.' The note's own summary records it as 'the named origin of the decomposition Gao et al. (2022, arXiv:2210.10760) apply to reward-model overoptimization' -- and Gao is already source [54] in the report. Grep confirms zero occurrences of 'Goodhart' in draft-a.md, draft-b.md, draft-c.md and the final report.
findings.recommendation: Add two sentences to RANK 10, adjacent to the existing Gao/Elimination-7 reframing. State that the paper's under-named diagnosis is Manheim & Garrabrant's Extremal Goodhart (Model Insufficiency), quote the sub-case definition, and note that this supplies the lineage Gao's scaling law sits in -- so citing Gao without Manheim cites the application rather than the category. Tag it FOLD-INTO-THIS-PAPER / CHEAP alongside the Fannjiang reframing, since it costs one citation and gives the paper a named category for its central mechanism claim. Add a source entry for arXiv:1803.04585.

findings.location: Deliverable (iii), RANK 9 table, row 9 ('A graded three-arm battery varying distributional mismatch, upgrading the binary inversion count into a dose-response curve')
findings.issue: This is the only row in the RANK 9 experiment table carrying no citation at all. The query is explicit: for an under-executed result, 'name the experiment and cite the work that motivates it.' The vault holds the exact methodological template -- and draft-a had it ('a three-arm graded battery in the style of BCQ'), which the synthesizer dropped. An unattributed experiment recommendation in a report whose entire subject is citation fidelity is a self-inflicted wound.
findings.evidence: Vault note `181202900-off-policy-deep-reinforcement-learning-without-exploration` (Fujimoto, Meger & Precup, BCQ, ICML 2019), tagged this pass. Summary: names and decomposes 'extrapolation error' into absent data / model bias / training mismatch and 'demonstrates it POSITIVELY (not by elimination) via a graded battery of three dataset-construction protocols (final-buffer, concurrent, imitation) that vary how much the batch's action distribution diverges from the evaluation policy, showing value-estimate divergence scales with that divergence. This graded-battery methodology, not any single finding, is the reusable template for converting the offline-MBO paper's inversion result from an anecdote into a dose-response curve.' `research/temp/coverage-gaps.md` lists BCQ among the eight primaries covering 'Under-executed: elimination -> mechanism' (Well-covered). draft-a.md line 336 contains 'a three-arm graded battery in the style of BCQ'; the final report has zero BCQ hits.
findings.recommendation: Restore the attribution in RANK 9 row 9: name BCQ's three-protocol construction (final-buffer / concurrent / imitation) as the template, note that BCQ demonstrates extrapolation error positively rather than by elimination -- which is precisely the conversion the paper's seven negatives need -- and add arXiv:1812.02900 to the source list. One clause plus one citation.

findings.location: Deliverable (iii), RANK 9 table, row 8 ('The double-dissociation transplant')
findings.issue: The report's single cleanest causal-test recommendation cites only SNGP [26] and DUQ [27] -- neither of which is a deep-kernel paper. The two sources that actually establish the predicted double dissociation (unconstrained deep kernel fails; bi-Lipschitz-constrained variant recovers) are in the vault and uncited. The report also grades the item EXPENSIVE / FOLLOW-UP while the vault note grades the same arm as the natural CHEAP transplant, so the cost tag may be miscalibrated against the corpus.
findings.evidence: Vault note `151102222-deep-kernel-learning` (Wilson, Hu, Salakhutdinov & Xing, AISTATS 2016), tagged this pass AND tagged `positive-mechanism-candidate`. Summary calls DKL 'the textbook natural interpolant between a plain GP and a neural network, and hence the natural CHEAP transplant arm for isolating whether the offline-MBO paper's GP-vs-ensemble gap is about having a GP posterior per se or about what feature space that posterior operates over.' Companion vault note `on-feature-collapse-and-deep-kernel-learning-for-single-forward-pass-uncertainty` (van Amersfoort et al., DUE, arXiv:2102.11409) supplies the failure half verbatim: an unconstrained deep-kernel GP (GPDNN) is 'certain even far away from the training data' unless the feature extractor is bi-Lipschitz/spectral-normalized. draft-a.md line 336 named 'Deep Kernel Learning plus a bi-Lipschitz-constrained deterministic-uncertainty model'; the final report has zero hits for 'deep kernel' and zero for 'feature collapse'.
findings.recommendation: In RANK 9 row 8, name Deep Kernel Learning (Wilson et al., AISTATS 2016, arXiv:1511.02222) as the transplant arm and DUE (van Amersfoort et al., arXiv:2102.11409) as the source establishing that an unconstrained deep kernel inherits the ensemble's failure while a bi-Lipschitz constraint restores distance-awareness. Add both to the source list. Also reconsider the EXPENSIVE tag in light of the vault's CHEAP-if-scoped assessment, or state explicitly why the report grades it higher.

findings.location: Deliverable (iii), RANK 1 ('Interpret the interaction term') and RANK 1b ('Report the formal simple-effects table')
findings.issue: The report states that the paper's bibliography contains 'zero design-of-experiments citations' and then supplies only two open sources ([58] NIST OFAT, [59] Box). The vault holds four further DOE authorities tagged to this pass, two of which are directly on-point for claims RANK 1 and RANK 1b make without support. RANK 1b proposes a formal simple-effects decomposition with no procedural citation whatsoever, and RANK 1's central reason (2) -- 'optimizer choice has a small marginal effect and a substantial conditional one' -- has a canonical published instance of exactly that pattern in the vault that the report does not cite.
findings.evidence: (a) `34-factorial-anova-simple-effects-statistics-libretexts` (Statistics LibreTexts §3.4, tagged `locus-interaction-grounding`, `simple-effects`): 'When researchers find an interaction it suggests that the main effects may be a bit misleading,' and whenever an interaction is detected researchers 'need to conduct additional analyses' -- simple-effects analyses at each level of the other factor -- because averaging across levels can cancel a real effect. This is the exact procedural warrant RANK 1b asserts without citing. (b) `5471-full-factorial-example` (NIST/SEMATECH §5.4.7.1, 20,671 chars): a worked 2^5 factorial stating 'Note that large interactions can obscure main effects' and reporting that Speed 'plays a role in almost every significant interaction term, but is the least important main effect on its own' -- structurally identical to the paper's optimizer axis (eta-sq_opt 0.005-0.036 against eta-sq_inter 0.146-0.165). (c) `532-how-do-you-select-and-scale-the-process-variables` (NIST §5.3.2), also tagged. Grep: '5.4.7' appears zero times in all three drafts and the final.
findings.recommendation: Two surgical additions. In RANK 1, after reason (2), cite NIST §5.4.7.1's worked full-factorial finding that a factor can be the least important main effect while dominating the interaction structure -- this converts the paper's optimizer null from an anomaly into a textbook-recognised pattern with a canonical reference. In RANK 1b, cite the simple-effects source for the procedure itself ('once an interaction is significant, main effects can mislead and simple effects are the standard remedy'), which the report currently asserts on its own authority. Add both URLs to the source list.

findings.location: Deliverable (i), item M (the per-task normalizer paragraph), and Deliverable (iii) RANK 5
findings.issue: The report asserts that 'rank statistics are pool-dependent' and cites Benavoli [43], who is about post-hoc tests on mean-ranks, not about aggregation-pool sensitivity. The primary that owns pool-dependence -- and that is the acknowledged origin of the 'nonexploitability' criterion Jordan et al. [63] invoke in the very sentence before -- is in the vault, tagged this pass, and uncited. This also under-supports RANK 5, whose leave-one-task-out check is literally a redundancy/pool-sensitivity analysis presented without the literature that names it.
findings.evidence: Vault note `180602643-re-evaluating-evaluation` (Balduzzi, Tuyls, Perolat & Graepel, NeurIPS 2018), tagged this pass. Summary quotes: 'measuring performance by uniformly averaging over tasks in a benchmark suite is sensitive to the set of tasks that are included in the suite. Including redundant tasks, whether consciously or not, can easily skew average performance in favor of or against particular agents,' with a worked example where duplicating one agent shifts other agents' Elo by 63 points despite no change in underlying skill. The note explicitly records Balduzzi as 'the origin of the nonexploitative aggregation criterion Jordan et al. (2020) cite when critiquing min-max normalization' -- Jordan is already source [63]. Grep: 'Balduzzi' and 'Nash averaging' appear zero times in all three drafts and the final.
findings.recommendation: One sentence in (i).M, at the 'Ranks are not a clean escape' clause: attribute pool-dependence to Balduzzi et al., quote the redundant-task sensitivity line, and note that Jordan's non-exploitability criterion descends from it -- so the report's two normalizer authorities share a root. One clause in RANK 5 noting that the leave-one-task-out check is the paper's de facto redundancy-sensitivity analysis in Balduzzi's sense. Add arXiv:1806.02643 to the source list.

findings.location: Terminal section 'What I could not verify and why', subsection A (paywalled or access-blocked primaries)
findings.issue: The report concedes that 'Montgomery's Design and Analysis of Experiments Ch. 5 could not be reached; the positive design-of-experiments framing rests instead on the NIST handbook [58] and Box [59].' The vault holds a fetched, tagged, quotable Montgomery-derived source that the report does not acknowledge. The concession is broader than the corpus warrants, which matters because this terminal section is a contracted deliverable whose accuracy is itself an audit claim.
findings.evidence: Vault note `montgomery-design-and-analysis-of-experiments-sasjmp-supplement-excerpt-ofat-vs` (5,513 chars, tagged this pass and `locus-interaction-grounding`). Summary: 'Official SAS/JMP companion excerpt to Montgomery's DAOE textbook: quotes that OFAT analysis fails to reveal whether a factor's effect on the target depends on other factors (interaction), explicitly citing Montgomery's book; Ch.5 Introduction to Factorial Designs starts p.77 of supplement, but full Montgomery Ch.5 prose not independently verified (excerpt truncated).'
findings.recommendation: Narrow the concession rather than delete it: state that the official SAS/JMP companion excerpt to Montgomery was obtained and quotes the OFAT-cannot-detect-interactions point with attribution to the textbook, but that Montgomery's own Ch. 5 prose was not independently verified. Optionally cite the excerpt in RANK 1 as a third DOE authority. One clause in the terminal section; the honesty posture improves rather than degrades.

findings.location: Deliverable (i), item B, the 'A correction this audit owes itself' paragraph (the withdrawal of the 'nobody owns the trapped-at-the-data failure mode' claim)
findings.issue: The withdrawal paragraph sweeps TuRBO, Fan and GIBO and then names Yarotsky as closest prior art. One further local-BO source, verified first-hand in this pass and named in the coverage-gaps file as covering exactly this thread, is missing -- and it makes the argument stronger rather than weaker, because it is a second, independent convergence proof for the very algorithm family the paper's paralysis framing would need to contradict.
findings.evidence: Vault note `230515572-the-behavior-and-convergence-of-local-bayesian-optimization` (Wu, Kim, Garnett & Gardner, NeurIPS 2023), tagged this pass. Summary: 'Cited by Fan et al. as ref [34] for the GIBO convergence proof (Lemma 15) that Fan et al.'s own Theorem 1 builds on... Provides the first rigorous convergence-rate analysis of GIBO in noiseless and noisy settings... Does not use the terms stuck, trust region, offline, or distance-aware anywhere; contains no locally maximal at the data framing. This is a convergence-guarantee paper (local BO DOES progress and converge), not a stalling/failure-mode paper.' `research/temp/coverage-gaps.md` lists 'Wu et al. local-BO convergence' among the sources covering 'Under-explained: LCB paralysis / frozen cells'. Grep: 'Wu et' appears zero times in all three drafts and the final.
findings.recommendation: One clause in (i).B's correction paragraph: note that Wu et al.'s independent convergence-rate analysis of GIBO -- the lemma Fan's Theorem 1 builds on -- likewise contains no stalling vocabulary, so the local-BO literature as a whole proves progress rather than paralysis. This tightens the vocabulary sweep the paragraph claims to have run and closes the 'did you check the whole family?' objection. Add arXiv:2305.15572 to the source list.

findings.location: N6 Verdict, section B ('The queries, run verbatim') / the three adversarial regions paragraph, and the (ii) Kills table
findings.issue: The N6 verdict names only Kudela & Dobrovsky [8] and Gorissen [9] as the adversarial-region results, but the vault holds two further first-hand-verified region negatives from this same pass, both tagged `n6-not-a-kill`, and neither appears anywhere in the report. Since N6 is existential and the query demands the verdict be reported 'with the queries', a region sweep that under-reports its own verified negatives is weaker than it needs to be -- particularly one of these, which declines the optimizer crossing explicitly and is therefore a cleaner near-miss than a bare null.
findings.evidence: (a) `mukhtar-2023-ml-comparative-analysis-surrogate-models-cfd-heliyon` (tagged `n6-kill-hunt`, `n6-not-a-kill`, `doe`, `near-miss`): 'Mukhtar et al. (Heliyon 2023) compare PR vs Kriging surrogates for CFD ventilation design but use only ONE optimizer (Shifted Hammersley Sampling), explicitly declining to run the two other available optimizers (MOGA, NLPQL) -- fails the optimizer-crossing requirement. Factorial/main effect/interaction hits are DOE-sampling and physical-variable-sensitivity homonyms.' (b) `efficient-parameter-importance-analysis-via-ablation-with-surrogates-proceedings` (Biedenkapp et al., AAAI-17, full PDF pulled and grepped): 'exactly ONE surrogate model class used throughout (random forest EPM) -- fails condition (a)... VERDICT: does not extend or kill N6.' Grep: 'Mukhtar' and 'Biedenkapp' appear zero times in all three drafts and the final.
findings.recommendation: Add one sentence to the adversarial-regions paragraph in N6 section B (or a row to the section C near-miss table for Mukhtar): a second CFD surrogate comparison had two further optimizers available and explicitly declined to run them, so conjunct (b) fails by the authors' own stated choice rather than by absence -- the strongest form of a regional negative. Note Biedenkapp's ablation-with-surrogates as a one-surrogate-class analysis-method comparison, since it is the paper a reviewer familiar with the Hutter/Freiburg lineage is most likely to raise. Add both to the source list.

findings.location: Whole draft — chiefly the interaction between N6 section D/E, the (ii) Kills table, deliverable (i).M, and deliverable (iii) RANK 5
findings.issue: The report is 109KB against the pipeline's 45-55KB top-performer norm, and the excess is concentrated in three arguments each stated at full length two or three times rather than once with cross-references. The RaM Table-3 near-miss analysis is fully restated in N6 section C (table row), section D (three-ground table), section E (fix list) and the (ii) Kills table -- the 0.027-vs-0.577 eta-squared pair appears three separate times with its full framing. The min-max normalizer critique is stated at full length in (i).M and again at full length in RANK 5, with two further partial restatements as qualifications inside RANK 1 and RANK 2 ('normaliz' occurs 20 times). The Rahaman/width-at-fixed-depth scope limitation is argued in (i).G and re-argued in the RANK 9 row 7 entry.
findings.evidence: File size 109KB, 15,707 words. Phrase counts in the final report: '0.027' x3, '0.577' x3, 'min–max' x4, 'normaliz' x20, 'seven eliminations' x5, 'operating-point' x4, 'RaM' x65. The three angle drafts totalled ~41,000 words and the synthesis retained ~14,000 of distinct content plus these restatements.
findings.recommendation: Tighten three passages without cutting evidence. (1) In the (ii) Kills table, reduce the RaM row to its verdict plus a pointer to N6 section D, deleting the restated 4-versus-5 breakdown and the eta-squared pair. (2) In RANK 5, delete the re-derivation of why the endogenous min-max form is outlier-exploitable (already fully argued in (i).M) and keep only the new material -- the 33-of-33 robustness result, the FLAW_LEDGER/scripts_eta_robustness discovery, and the Griewank self-correction. (3) In RANK 9 row 7, reduce the depth-sweep entry to one line pointing at (i).G. These three cuts remove roughly 900 words of pure restatement and cost no evidence.

findings.location: Opening verdict block (lines 3-9) against N6 section A and deliverable (iii) section A
findings.issue: The opening block states the HIGH-to-trust / NIL-to-results severity split and the 'pair of positive findings the paper already owns and does not report' in near-final form, then N6 section A restates the CONFIRMED NONE-FOUND verdict with the same paywalled-lead caveat, and (iii) section A restates the pairing argument with the same 'each survives exactly what the other fails' phrasing. This is front-loading rather than duplication of a conclusion, but the verbatim phrase reuse inflates length without adding evidence.
findings.evidence: 'Each survives exactly the challenge the other fails' (line 9) versus 'Each survives exactly what the other fails' (line 259). 'CONFIRMED NONE-FOUND' with the paywalled-lead disclosure appears at line 3 and again at line 17 with the same justification ('disclosed here rather than in the terminal section / named inside the verdict rather than buried').
findings.recommendation: Differentiate the two paywalled-lead statements: keep the disclosure in the opening block and reduce the section A restatement to the operative claim about where residual risk is disclosed, without re-arguing why. Reword one of the two 'survives exactly what the other fails' sentences so the opening states the recommendation (report both together) and (iii).A states the mechanism (the crossed survival table). Roughly 120 words.
